We investigate the influence of stellar mass on photoevaporation within protoplanetary disks, utilizing a new, self-consistent model that accounts for the disk's vertical structure. Our findings indicate that the mass-loss rate is highly sensitive to stellar mass, rising by a factor of 100 between 0.1 and 10 solar masses. This trend aligns with observations of the disk lifetime distribution, which shows a strong correlation with stellar mass. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the disk's vertical structure plays a critical role in regulating mass loss, with the rate increasing by a factor of 10 when the disk is modeled as a flared slab rather than a flat one.

This study introduces a new class of explicit generalized-$\alpha$ time integration methods designed for structural dynamics, specifically tailored for isogeometric analysis. These approaches leverage the inherent smoothness of isogeometric basis functions to achieve higher-order accuracy. The paper details the development of these schemes and provides numerical results demonstrating their performance.

This study investigates the decay of a Bose polaron within a one-dimensional twin-well system containing a single impurity immersed in a Bose-Einstein condensate. We examine how the polaron's lifetime responds to variations in intra- and interband excitations of the condensate, alongside changes in the polaron's energy and momentum. Our findings indicate that the decay rate is governed by the energy gap between the polaron and the condensate's ground state, as well as the momentum transfer involved in the decay process.

This study addresses the challenge of optimizing logistics for disaster relief efforts, specifically focusing on the efficient distribution of aid supplies to affected populations. The proposed methodology employs a multi-phase stochastic optimization framework designed to determine the most effective allocation of resources. The initial phase involves a stochastic optimization process aimed at establishing the optimal number of supply depots and their geographic locations. The subsequent phase utilizes a multi-commodity network flow model to calculate the ideal quantity of supplies to deliver to each depot. The final phase applies a stochastic optimization approach to determine the most efficient routes for transporting aid from depots to the ultimate recipients. The paper concludes by presenting computational results derived from applying this integrated framework to a real-world case study.

Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) are currently detecting low-frequency gravitational waves (GWs) from the stochastic background, with the NANOGrav collaboration having recently reported a compelling signal. While the standard interpretation attributes this signal to a stochastic background from merging supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs), an alternative hypothesis suggests it originates from the eccentricity of the Milky Way's Galactic bar. This study utilizes the \texttt{gwsky} package to generate PTA signals from merging SMBHBs and Galactic bar models, incorporating post-Newtonian (PN) corrections up to 2.5th order. We evaluate the accuracy and computational costs of these signals across various PN orders and compare them against the standard Newtonian approximation. Our findings indicate that while 2.5th-order PN corrections are essential for accurately modeling the eccentricity of SMBHBs, they are not strictly necessary for modeling the Galactic bar. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the computational expense of generating these signals increases significantly with higher PN orders.

This paper introduces a novel approach to analyzing global programming contests by leveraging web scraping techniques. We detail the construction of a massive dataset comprising over 100,000 individual submissions from more than 10,000 participants across 1,000 competitions. Our analysis examines the temporal patterns of problem-solving, specifically focusing on the time taken to solve each challenge. Furthermore, we investigate the correlation between a participant's rank and their submission timing, as well as the relationship between a problem's difficulty and its solution duration.

This study introduces a new on-chip analysis method for high-dissipation liquids, utilizing a 750 GHz to 1100 GHz millimeter-wave waveguide. The waveguide's design is optimized for this specific frequency band, featuring a 100 μm gap between the silicon nitride substrate and the top silicon layer. The device employs a 100 μm diameter hole in the top silicon layer to hold the liquid sample, with a 100 μm diameter silicon nitride membrane positioned 10 μm below the sample to ensure precise volume control. The waveguide's resonant frequency is determined by the sample's dielectric properties, allowing for the measurement of the liquid's dielectric constant and loss tangent. The paper details the design and fabrication of the waveguide, presents experimental results for water, and compares these findings with literature data.

The global pandemic of COVID-19 has resulted in over 100,000 fatalities and more than 10 million confirmed cases. While the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) have issued guidelines for prevention and mitigation, the rapid evolution of the virus and the emergence of new variants have rendered these strategies increasingly ineffective. To address this, we propose AIRSENSE-TO-ACT, a framework designed to develop effective strategies for preventing and mitigating COVID-19. This approach leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI) and multi-source data analysis to create a comprehensive, adaptable, and scalable system. The framework's core components include: (1) an AI-driven data collection and analysis module that aggregates data from diverse sources such as news, social media, and government reports; (2) an AI-powered strategy generation module that utilizes machine learning to identify patterns and predict outbreaks; and (3) an AI-based strategy execution module that employs natural language processing to communicate actionable advice to the public. By integrating these elements, AIRSENSE-TO-ACT offers a robust and flexible solution for managing the ongoing COVID-19 crisis.

This study introduces a multi-scale Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) framework designed to simulate fluid-structure interactions (FSI) involving deformable bodies. The proposed method employs a hybrid particle system that integrates both standard and high-resolution particles. Standard particles are utilized to model the fluid domain, whereas high-resolution particles are dedicated to capturing the deformation of the solid structure. The fluid-structure interface is defined by the spatial overlap between these two particle types. The fluid dynamics are governed by the weakly compressible SPH (WCSPH) formulation, while the solid deformation is tracked using a Lagrangian approach. The fluid and solid components are coupled through a novel, robust, and efficient algorithm that ensures the seamless exchange of information between the hybrid particles. The method's efficacy is validated through a series of numerical tests, including a dam-break scenario, a wave tank simulation, and a wave impact on a floating body.

This review examines the topological attributes of nodal surfaces within momentum space, specifically focusing on the Berry curvature and Berry phase. We explore how these topological features are realized in photonic systems and other platforms, alongside their associated physical phenomena.

This report outlines the findings from the evaluation of event generators conducted during the second half of the 2018 HL-LHC Computing Assessment Stage. The analysis focuses on the computational resources required to generate data for the two primary LHC physics programs, specifically within the context of the HL-LHC environment.

This paper examines the partial averages operator defined as $A_Nf(x)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^Nf(x\lambda^n)$, where $\lambda>1$ is a fixed real number. We demonstrate that the supremum of the $L^p$ operator norms for $1<p<\infty$ is finite, and we establish a characteristic invariant under dilation for the measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, where $\hat{\mu}(\lambda)=0$.

This finding is derived from a comprehensive analysis of the 12CO(1-0) emission line, utilizing data from the APEX telescope and the IRAM 30m radio telescope. The study focuses on the Galactic disk extending from approximately 10 to 16 kiloparsecs from the center, an area where the rotation curve remains nearly flat. The analysis reveals that the 12CO(1-0) emission line exhibits a distinct, narrow, and symmetric profile, which is notably narrower than the line widths observed in the inner Galaxy. This study examines the relationship between the salaries and services of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Macedonia (ARM) by analyzing the evolution of remuneration and benefits for officers and enlisted personnel from 1991 to 2019. The analysis utilizes data from official sources, including the Ministry of Defense, the State Statistical Office, and the National Bank of the Republic of Macedonia. The findings indicate that while the nominal salaries and services of the Armed Forces have increased significantly over the past three decades, their real value has declined. This decline is primarily driven by inflation, which has eroded purchasing power. The study concludes that the current compensation system fails to adequately reflect the services rendered by the Armed Forces and recommends implementing a more effective and sustainable remuneration framework.

This study investigates the collective behavior of dense, disordered collections of polar active matter, specifically examining the influence of particle shape and size polydispersity. We demonstrate that the collective dynamics of such systems are governed by the interplay between the active force and the degree of polydispersity. Specifically, we identify a novel phase characterized by a disordered structure with a static, non-zero order parameter, which emerges when polydispersity is sufficiently high.

This study investigates the semileptonic decays of doubly charmed baryons, specifically $\Xi_{cc}^{\pm} \to \Xi_{c}^{0, \pm} \ell^{\pm} \nu_{\ell}$ and $\Omega_{cc}^{\pm} \to \Omega_{c}^{0, \pm} \ell^{\pm} \nu_{\ell}$, utilizing the pouch model. We calculate the relevant form factors and subsequently derive the partial decay widths for these semileptonic processes.

This study introduces a new approach to estimating an agent's location within a scene by leveraging embodied conversation. The method utilizes a neural network to predict the agent's position based on dialogue, with training data derived from the Embodied Conversational Home (ECH) dataset. The model is designed to handle both single-turn and multi-turn interactions. Evaluation results indicate that the model achieves strong performance, with a mean absolute error of 0.8 meters on the ECH dataset.

Vibration analysis is a widely used technique for assessing the health of rotating machinery. Typically, this process involves selecting specific frequency bands to evaluate vibration levels. However, the choice of these bands is often subjective and relies on the operator's expertise, which can lead to inconsistent results. This paper introduces a novel method called the Band Significance Factor (BSF), designed to automatically determine the most relevant frequency bands for vibration assessment. The proposed method is validated using both simulated and real-world data. The results demonstrate that BSF effectively identifies the most significant frequency bands, thereby enhancing the accuracy of vibration evaluation.

This study employs muon-spin relaxation and rotation techniques to examine the superconducting ground states of the noncentrosymmetric compounds CaTSi$_3$ (where T = Ir or Pt). Our findings reveal that both materials exhibit a single superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) of approximately 2.5 K, with no indication of a secondary transition. Furthermore, the muon-spin relaxation rate remains constant below $T_c$, suggesting that the superconducting state is homogeneous. These observations imply that the effects of spin-orbit coupling in these noncentrosymmetric superconductors are minimal.

This paper introduces a novel approach to solving high-dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations, which are fundamental to optimal response control. The method relies on a specific set of basis functions known as sparse grid attributes. We demonstrate that this framework is highly effective for addressing the "curse of dimensionality" inherent in HJB equations. The authors provide a rigorous convergence analysis and validate the method's efficacy through various numerical examples.

This study introduces a framework for modeling and regulating multi-energy systems, which are pivotal to the transition toward decarbonization. The proposed approach integrates diverse energy carriers—such as electricity, heat, and gas—into a unified system, enabling the analysis of their interdependencies. The authors develop a linearized model that captures the dynamics of these interactions and demonstrates its application in regulating the system. The research further illustrates the model's utility through a case study of a multi-energy system, specifically examining how it facilitates the integration of renewable energy sources.

This study introduces a rapid magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique for mapping heat distribution within a gas-solid stationary bed. The method employs a specialized pulse sequence that combines a low-power radiofrequency (RF) pulse with a gradient echo to generate a temperature-sensitive image. By utilizing a low-power RF pulse, the technique minimizes the flip angle, thereby reducing the heat deposited in the sample and enabling the acquisition of multiple images in quick succession. The resulting images are corrected for magnetic field inhomogeneities and subsequently fitted to a heat diffusion model to determine the thermal diffusivity of the gas-solid mixture. The validity of this approach was confirmed through experiments on a packed bed of glass beads, where the measured thermal diffusivity aligned well with theoretical predictions.

We introduce a theoretical framework for superconductivity that accounts for thermal fluctuations and disorder, specifically addressing the reentrant superconductivity observed in UTe$_2$ near its critical temperature. This model posits that disorder induces a finite superconducting gap, while thermal fluctuations generate a second, vanishingly small gap. The interplay between these two gaps results in a reentrant phase transition, a phenomenon that can be experimentally verified through specific heat measurements.

Ultra-wideband (UWB) technology is a promising solution for high-precision ranging and localization, yet its performance is heavily influenced by the specific radio configuration. This paper introduces a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework designed to automatically optimize UWB physical layer (PHY) settings in real-time. The proposed method dynamically adjusts transmission parameters based on the surrounding environment to maximize ranging accuracy. We evaluated the system using a DRL agent trained on a simulated UWB channel, which was then tested in a real-world scenario. Results indicate that the DRL agent successfully learns to identify optimal configurations for various environments, achieving a 10% reduction in ranging error compared to a baseline approach.

This study examines the k-median grouping problem within the context of discrete Fréchet and Hausdorff metrics. We present a polynomial-time algorithm for k-median grouping using the Hausdorff metric, which is proven to be 2-approximate. Additionally, we demonstrate that the k-median grouping problem is NP-hard when formulated under the discrete Fréchet metric.

Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is a rapidly expanding field that has garnered significant attention from both academia and industry. This paper introduces a novel MARL framework grounded in primal-dual optimization, which leverages the inherent structure of the multi-agent Markov decision process (MDP) to derive a closed-form update rule for the joint action distribution. This approach is designed to maximize the expected return of the system. We demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves a convergence rate of $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ regarding the optimality gap, where $T$ represents the number of iterations. Furthermore, we provide numerical experiments that validate the effectiveness of our method.

This study introduces a novel approach for reconstructing sparse initial conditions in partial differential equations (PDEs) using low-rank tensor methods. The proposed technique integrates the tensor train (TT) framework with a deep learning architecture to recover these initial states from observed data. The deep learning component is trained on synthetic data generated by solving PDEs via isogeometric analysis (IGA), leveraging the tensor train representation to enforce sparsity. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through numerical experiments involving the 2D wave equation and the 3D heat equation.

This study introduces a novel air quality monitoring system that employs a compact chart of sensors to gather data through drive-through sampling. The system utilizes a regressive facility location algorithm to determine optimal sensor placements, ensuring that the selected sites capture the most representative air quality data. The proposed approach is evaluated against a baseline method that relies on random sensor positioning.

This paper presents a new construction of the Weil representation for the generalized linear group $G_n$ (defined over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$) across the ring $R = \mathbb{F}_q[t]/(t^N)$, utilizing a specific two-sided involution. The involution is given by the formula $\overline{a_0 + a_1t + \dots + a_{N-1}t^{N-1}} = a_0 + a_1t + \dots + a_{N-1}t^{N-1}$.

The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has enabled the development of AI-driven video generation systems capable of producing high-quality, realistic content. These systems are increasingly utilized across diverse fields, including entertainment, education, and marketing. This paper reviews the current landscape of AI-driven video generation, focusing on the underlying technologies, their practical applications, and the associated ethical concerns.

This study examines the quantum dynamics of ions held within combined quadrupole and octopole ion traps. We introduce a novel class of squeezed coherent states representing the system's motion, which are constructed using a specific set of creation and annihilation operators. These operators are derived from the eigenfunctions of the Hamiltonian, which are solved using the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation. Furthermore, we calculate the expectation values of the system's position and momentum for these newly defined states.

Neuroscience frameworks are increasingly utilized to address intricate challenges in artificial intelligence, yet their application is hindered by the necessity for extensive hyper-parameter tuning. This study introduces a novel approach to identify optimal hyper-parameter configurations for these frameworks by employing meta-learning techniques. We demonstrate that this method effectively identifies superior hyper-parameters for neuroscience models, including those used in image classification and the analysis of brain connectivity. Furthermore, we illustrate that this strategy can be applied to optimize hyper-parameters for large-scale neuroscience simulations running on high-performance computing systems.

Camouflaged object segmentation (COS) is a difficult computer vision task that involves separating objects from their backgrounds when they share similar colors, textures, and shapes. This paper introduces Camouflaged Object Segmentation In-The-Wild (COSITW), a new dataset comprising 1,000 images featuring 1,500 object instances. COSITW is the first dataset to include both object-level and instance-level annotations. To address this challenge, we propose a novel method that integrates a multi-scale feature fusion module with a multi-task learning framework. The multi-scale module combines features from various levels to enhance the model's ability to detect camouflaged objects, while the multi-task component simultaneously performs segmentation and classification to boost overall accuracy. We also developed a dedicated benchmark toolkit to facilitate the evaluation of different approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the COSITW dataset.

This study examines the impact of Lorentz violation on superconductivity, utilizing a relativistic framework for the Ginzburg-Landau free energy. We analyze how a CPT-violating background vector field influences the critical temperature and the London penetration depth. Furthermore, we investigate the effects of this background vector field on the superconducting state, specifically examining how it alters the coherence length and the critical magnetic field. Finally, we discuss the implications of these findings for the experimental detection of Lorentz violation in superconductors.

This study examines the application of crowdsourcing to identify and validate errors within AI systems. We introduce a novel framework that leverages human intuition to pinpoint AI failures, subsequently employing crowdsourced verification to substantiate these findings. Our approach was tested on a practical case involving a computer vision model designed to detect COVID-19 from chest X-rays. The results demonstrate that this method is both effective and cost-efficient, successfully uncovering and validating 100% of the AI's errors.

This paper introduces a novel stochastic routing strategy for object recognition, designed to enhance the accuracy of deep neural networks. The method routes input images to a randomly selected subset of detectors, where each detector is chosen with a specific probability. The final classification is determined by aggregating the outputs from this chosen subset. Theoretically, we demonstrate that this approach yields higher accuracy than deterministic routing, which assigns every image to all detectors. Furthermore, we provide a practical algorithm for selecting the optimal subset of detectors and the corresponding probabilities. Experimental results on the CIFAR-10 dataset confirm that this method surpasses both deterministic routing and standard ensemble techniques.

Adversarial training has become a standard method for enhancing the robustness of deep neural networks (DNNs) against malicious attacks. However, this approach often suffers from catastrophic overfitting, a phenomenon where the model excessively lowers its loss on adversarial examples at the expense of its accuracy on clean data. This study investigates the root causes of such overfitting and introduces a novel solution called ZeroGrad. The research reveals that catastrophic overfitting stems from the model's tendency to over-rely on specific features that are easily manipulated by adversarial perturbations. To counteract this, we propose ZeroGrad, a technique that constrains the gradient norm of the loss function during the adversarial training process. This constraint forces the model to utilize a broader range of features rather than focusing on a few easily exploited ones. Empirical results demonstrate that ZeroGrad effectively mitigates catastrophic overfitting across various architectures and datasets, achieving superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

We demonstrate that the Thakurta metric, which was previously suggested to describe the spacetime of a charged black hole, is actually incorrect. This error has led to flawed constraints on primordial black holes (PBHs) derived from LIGO-Virgo observations of gravitational waves. We show that these constraints remain unchanged when corrected.

This study examines how persistent asset changes influence a specific class of hybrid-inspired optimization techniques, which integrate concepts from both evolutionary algorithms and swarm intelligence. The research focuses on the impact of such changes on the performance of the hybrid algorithm known as the Hybrid Genetic Algorithm with Particle Swarm Optimization (HGA-PSO). The analysis reveals that HGA-PSO is highly sensitive to persistent asset changes, a finding that is corroborated by empirical results.

We introduce BTS, a bootstrappable fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) framework that leverages the Gaussian elimination method to achieve bootstrapping. This approach enables the evaluation of linear operations on ciphertexts, thereby extending the capabilities of existing bootstrappable schemes like BFV and CKKS to support linear computations. Our implementation of BTS demonstrates a bootstrapping latency of 1.2 seconds, which is 1.5 times faster than the BFV baseline. Furthermore, we present a novel bootstrapping strategy for BFV that utilizes the ternary property of plaintexts to enhance efficiency. This method yields a bootstrapping latency of 0.6 seconds, representing a 2.0-fold improvement over the standard BFV approach.

This paper introduces a solvable model for random matrix ensembles featuring a logarithmic confining potential. The model's partition function is expressed as a multiple contour integral, which is subsequently evaluated using the saddle-point method. This approach yields a closed-form expression for the limiting distribution of eigenvalues, which is then analyzed in detail.

We present a novel argument demonstrating that any theory permitting faster-than-light communication must allow for the decomposition of its joint probability distributions into a mixture of locally decomposable distributions. This result stands apart from Bell's theorem because it does not rely on statistical inequalities or the assumption of measurement independence.

By utilizing a single generator, the model achieves StyleGAN2-level image quality while producing videos that are more stable and realistic than those generated by GAN-V. The model's generator is a modified StyleGAN2 architecture that incorporates a new temporal attention mechanism, which integrates information from previous frames to enhance temporal consistency. Additionally, the model employs a new perceptual loss function to improve temporal consistency and a new adversarial loss function to enhance temporal coherence. This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to estimate the irradiation date of thermoluminescence (TL) materials. The approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to analyze TL glow curves, which are generated by heating samples to various temperatures and measuring the resulting light emission. The model was trained on a dataset comprising 1,000 glow curves from LiF:Mg,Ti crystals, covering irradiation dates from 1990 to 2018. The network achieved a mean absolute error of 1.1 years, with a 95% confidence interval of ±2.1 years. This performance surpasses that of the conventional TL fading method, which yielded a mean absolute error of 2.5 years and a 95% confidence interval of ±4.1 years.

This paper investigates the existence of solutions for a specific class of singular problems involving the p(x,y)-Laplacian, defined on a complete Riemannian manifold. The analysis incorporates a nonstandard growth condition characterized by a singularity at the origin, alongside a specific growth condition at infinity.

The Fastcat emulator, designed to simulate kilovoltage and megavoltage cone-beam CT (CBCT) systems, was developed to support the development and validation of image reconstruction algorithms. This study aimed to validate the emulator's accuracy by comparing its outputs against real CBCT scans from a Varian TrueBeam equipped with an On-Board Imager (OBI). A phantom containing a 10 cm diameter cylinder filled with a 10% barium sulfate solution was used for the experiment. The acquisition protocol involved a 360-degree rotation around the phantom, capturing 120 images at 1-degree intervals. The Fastcat emulator was configured to replicate the TrueBeam's kV and MV imaging parameters, including source-to-isocenter distance, detector geometry, and exposure settings. The resulting simulated and actual CBCT datasets were reconstructed using the Feldkamp-Davis-Hess algorithm (FDH). To assess the fidelity of the simulation, the root mean square error (RMSE) was calculated between the reconstructed images and the original phantom data. The findings revealed an RMSE of 0.011 for the kV simulation and 0.013 for the MV simulation, indicating a high degree of accuracy. These results confirm that the Fastcat emulator effectively models the TrueBeam's CBCT capabilities, thereby validating its utility for algorithm development and testing.

LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) is a popular method for generating explanations of machine learning predictions by training a surrogate model on perturbed data points near the target instance. However, LIME's reliance on random sampling can lead to unstable and inconsistent explanations. To address this, we introduce S-LIME (Stabilized-LIME), a new approach that enhances explanation stability by employing a Bayesian surrogate model. This model is trained on a dataset of perturbed samples, where each sample is assigned a weight reflecting its relevance to the target prediction. We evaluate S-LIME against the original LIME and two other baselines using both synthetic and real-world datasets. Results indicate that S-LIME produces significantly more stable explanations than the competing methods.

This study introduces a Bayesian framework designed to rectify classification errors by utilizing justification feedback. The model integrates this feedback to refine the categorization abilities of a learner. We evaluated the model's performance through simulations and a human-in-the-loop experiment, comparing it against a standard Bayesian approach that does not incorporate justification feedback. The results indicate that our model surpasses the standard baseline in both simulated environments and the real-world experiment.

The search for spin liquids has recently expanded to include materials with non-Abelian topological states, which are characterized by a continuous spectrum of excitations. This study reports on the crystal-field excitations in TbInO$_3$, a triangular-lattice compound that is a leading candidate for a spin liquid. Inelastic neutron scattering data reveal a continuous spectrum of crystal-field excitations, which is interpreted as a manifestation of a spin liquid state. Furthermore, the observed excitations display a vibronic pattern, indicating strong coupling between the crystal-field states and phonons. This coupling is analyzed in terms of a vibronic model, which is found to be consistent with the observed excitations. The results provide further evidence for the spin liquid state in TbInO$_3$ and highlight the importance of vibronic coupling in the material's properties.

This study examines the power-of-mean curvature flow, defined by the equation $\frac{d}{dt}x = -H^{p}\nu$, where $H$ represents the mean curvature, $\nu$ is the normal vector, and $p$ is a real parameter. We establish that for any $p \geq 1$, the flow preserves the convexity of a hypersurface. Furthermore, we demonstrate that when $p \in [0,1)$, the flow maintains convexity provided the initial hypersurface is sufficiently close to a sphere.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have become a cornerstone of deep learning, yet their training typically relies on gradient descent, a process that is computationally intensive and slow. This paper introduces a new approach to training CNNs by leveraging the convolution theorem, which allows convolutions to be performed as point-wise multiplications in the frequency domain. By utilizing the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to convert inputs and filters into the spectrum domain, we can execute these operations more efficiently. This method significantly accelerates the training process, reducing the computational cost of convolutions by a factor of 100 to 1,000. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this approach yields CNN performance comparable to that of standard gradient descent training.

This study introduces a multi-layer deep neural network designed to enhance image grouping. The proposed architecture employs a multi-layer framework that integrates both deep and shallow networks to facilitate the exchange of information between them. This approach allows the system to leverage the superior feature extraction capabilities of deep networks alongside the refined grouping performance of shallow models. Furthermore, the work presents a novel loss function specifically for image grouping tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy.

This paper introduces a framework for identifying organizational risks by leveraging knowledge networks and automated news analysis. The system comprises three primary components: a knowledge network that maps the interconnections among entities, a news analysis module that extracts relevant information from media reports, and a risk detection engine that synthesizes these elements to pinpoint organizational threats. The risk detection engine operates through two distinct phases: a learning phase, which utilizes a supervised machine learning algorithm to train on historical data, and an inference phase, which applies the trained model to detect risks in real-time. The study validates this framework using a dataset of 1,000 news articles concerning the 2016 U.S. presidential election, specifically focusing on the Trump campaign. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively identifies organizational risks with high precision.

This study introduces a novel approach to data classification grounded in topological data analysis. The methodology involves constructing a simplicial complex from the dataset, followed by the identification of its persistent homology features. The proposed classifier utilizes these topological characteristics to determine the category of new data points. The method's efficacy is validated through its successful application to the well-known Iris dataset.

Contrasimilarity, a concept introduced by the author in 2019, is defined as a relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and satisfies the condition that for any two elements $x$ and $y$, if $x$ is not contrasimilar to $y$, then $x$ must be similar to every element except $y$. This paper presents a game-theoretic framework for contrasimilarity, wherein two players, designated as the "not" player and the "similarity" player, determine the outcome based on whether the resulting graph is connected.

This work provides a concrete representation of the string 2-group, which serves as a higher-dimensional refinement of the structure group for principal bundles in string theory. We achieve this by utilizing the string Lie 2-algebra, which is the Malcev completion of the free nilpotent Lie 2-algebra of step 2 generated by a free associative algebra.

This study investigates the formation of rogue ion-acoustic waves within a double pair plasma comprising non-thermal, non-extensive electrons and positrons alongside non-thermal, non-extensive ions. By employing the reductive perturbation method, researchers derived the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation to analyze the nonlinear dynamics of these waves. The analysis reveals that the nonlinear coefficient in the KdV equation is highly sensitive to the non-extensive parameter, which consequently alters the amplitude of rogue waves. Furthermore, the study examines how variations in the non-extensive parameter influence the amplitude of these rogue waves.

The parametric decay instability (PDI) of Alfvén waves is a critical mechanism for energy transfer in magnetized plasmas, yet its occurrence in laboratory settings remains unobserved. This study investigates the PDI of Alfvén waves within a laboratory-relevant plasma environment using a hybrid kinetic-fluid model. The results indicate that the PDI can be triggered by Alfvén waves with a peak amplitude of approximately 0.01, provided the plasma satisfies specific criteria. The instability's growth rate is found to be proportional to the wave amplitude and inversely proportional to the ion cyclotron frequency. Furthermore, the PDI generates a spectrum of daughter waves, including both Alfvén and ion-acoustic modes.

This study examines the gravitational stability of threadlike molecular nebulae, accounting for ambipolar diffusion. We derive the dispersion relation for axisymmetric perturbations, revealing that ambipolar diffusion significantly influences the growth rates of unstable modes. Specifically, the instability growth rate is suppressed by ambipolar diffusion, and the critical mass required for instability is notably higher than in scenarios ignoring this effect. Furthermore, the instability growth rate is found to be independent of the magnetic field's strength.

We investigate the quantum Zeno and anti-Zeno effects within a two-level system coupled to a bosonic bath, specifically in the strong coupling regime. Our findings indicate that the system's decay rate is not a monotonically increasing or decreasing function of the measurement interval; rather, it exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on this interval, characterized by a minimum or maximum. This behavior is attributed to the interplay between the system's internal dynamics and the measurement process.

This study examines the thermal consistency of the two-dimensional Heisenberg model incorporating Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interactions and an asymmetric external field. By employing the spin-wave approximation, we derive the model's free energy and analyze its behavior across various temperatures and field strengths. Our findings indicate that the system exhibits a second-order phase transition, characterized by a shift from a ferromagnetic to a paramagnetic state.

This paper introduces a distributed path planning algorithm for quadrotor swarms, ensuring collision-free navigation through a 3D environment populated with static and dynamic obstacles. The proposed method employs a linear safe passage (LSP) framework to guarantee safety, utilizing a viability kernel to define the set of safe initial conditions. The algorithm operates by first calculating the viability kernel for the swarm, then determining the set of LSPs within this kernel, and finally assigning a specific LSP to each quadrotor. The study demonstrates that the algorithm is computationally efficient and scalable, with its performance validated through simulations.

This paper introduces CARLANE, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate unsupervised domain transfer (UDT) for path detection. CARLANE comprises 12 distinct datasets, each containing 100,000 annotated paths, and is built upon the CARLA simulator alongside real-world data from 11 varied locations. The benchmark assesses UDT performance using a standard pipeline that involves training a model on simulated data and testing it on real-world data. Our findings reveal that current state-of-the-art UDT methods fail to meet the rigorous demands of CARLANE, highlighting the necessity for more robust solutions. To address this, we propose a novel UDT approach that leverages a pre-trained backbone and employs a multi-task learning strategy to enhance the model's generalization capabilities.

Hydrogels are widely utilized in various applications, including drug delivery, tissue engineering, and the development of soft actuators. Their mechanical properties can be fine-tuned by incorporating particles, which also influence the swelling behavior of the polymer network. This study investigates how the addition of particles affects the contact angle of hydrogels. We demonstrate that particles can effectively reduce the contact angle, thereby enhancing adhesion to substrates. Furthermore, we propose a theoretical framework to explain this phenomenon, which aligns well with our experimental findings.

This study examines the relationship between student engagement and academic performance during the 2020–2021 school year, a period marked by the global COVID-19 pandemic and the transition to remote learning. Data were gathered from 1,000 students across 100 schools in the United States, utilizing the Student Engagement Survey (SES) to assess engagement levels and the Academic Performance Index (API) to measure achievement. The analysis reveals a significant positive correlation between engagement and performance, with a correlation coefficient of r = 0.31 (p < 0.001). Furthermore, the findings indicate that engagement levels were notably lower during the pandemic compared to pre-pandemic periods, while academic performance remained stable. These results underscore the critical role of student engagement in facilitating academic success, even within the challenging context of remote education.

This study introduces a novel technique for measuring wind speed at the planetary scale using Doppler radar data. The method relies on the assumption that the wind field exhibits a self-similar, fractal nature, meaning its statistical properties remain consistent across different spatial scales. By applying this principle, the wind field is modeled as a self-affine autoregressive process, allowing for the derivation of wind speed estimates from Doppler radar observations. The approach was validated using data from the L-band Doppler radar network in the United States, which covers the central and eastern regions of the country. The results demonstrate that the new method yields wind speed estimates that are comparable in accuracy to those produced by the National Weather Service's operational numerical weather prediction models.

We present a detailed analysis of the open cluster UBC 274, located in the Perseus Arm of the Milky Way. Utilizing Gaia EDR3 data, we identified 1,000 members and determined the cluster's distance to be 1.01 ± 0.02 kpc. By combining Gaia photometry with ground-based observations from the 2.5m Isaac Newton Telescope, we constructed a color-magnitude diagram (CMD) and derived the cluster's age as 1.0 ± 0.1 Gyr. Our investigation into the cluster's kinematics reveals a velocity dispersion of 1.2 km/s, indicating that UBC 274 is currently undergoing tidal disruption. Furthermore, we conducted a chemical abundance study using high-resolution spectroscopy of 10 cluster members, finding that they are metal-rich with [Fe/H] = +0.22 ± 0.05 dex. The derived abundances for alpha elements (Mg, Si, Ca, Ti) and iron-peak elements (Cr, Mn, Co, Ni) align with the solar ratios, while the [Al/Fe] ratio is notably enhanced at +0.22 ± 0.05 dex. These findings suggest that UBC 274 formed in the inner regions of the Galaxy, likely within the solar neighborhood.

This study examines the impact of using machine translation to improve bitext quality. We evaluate the effectiveness of applying a state-of-the-art neural translation system to refine noisy parallel data, specifically focusing on the resulting improvements in translation quality and the quality of the source texts. Our findings indicate that while the translation quality of the generated bitext improves, the source texts suffer degradation. Consequently, we conclude that relying solely on machine translation is insufficient for enhancing bitext quality.

We investigate the entanglement dynamics of a one-dimensional spin chain subjected to engineered dissipation, where a specific subset of spins is coupled to an auxiliary reservoir. Our findings reveal that the entanglement entropy of a subsystem initially rises logarithmically with its size; however, it eventually saturates to a constant value, adhering to an area law. This saturation level is governed by the subsystem's distance from the dissipative sites. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the steady-state entanglement entropy can be modulated by adjusting the coupling strength between the auxiliary reservoir and the spins.

We investigate the spin-orbit interaction within heterostructure flat bands formed by stacking transition metal dichalcogenides. Our analysis reveals that the spin-orbit coupling in these flat bands is significantly enhanced compared to that of isolated monolayers. This amplification stems from the strong hybridization between the monolayers, which generates a pronounced effective electric field perpendicular to the layers. Consequently, this interaction can be leveraged to engineer flat bands with tunable spin-orbit coupling strengths.

We examine the capabilities of quantum reservoir computing within constrained dimensional settings, specifically focusing on a single qubit subjected to a time-varying magnetic field. By utilizing a time-dependent field, we demonstrate that this qubit can function as a universal approximator for time-series data, effectively serving as a quantum reservoir. We further investigate the impact of environmental noise on the system's performance.

We propose a method to trap atoms using a gallium nitride (GaN) layer grown on a sapphire substrate, leveraging the material's intrinsic bandgap for optical confinement and its native surface for thermal management. This approach offers a viable pathway to achieve the high-temperature operation necessary for scalable, room-temperature quantum networks.

This paper presents a comparison of finite element methods for solving the Poisson equation, focusing on both Lagrange and mixed approaches. The study evaluates the accuracy of these methods by examining the error in the solution and its derivatives. The research utilizes the MFEM library, an open-source C++ toolkit for finite element analysis, to implement the algorithms.

This study investigates the dynamical behavior of a specific class of interacting dark energy models defined by the equation of state $w_{DE} = \omega_0 + \omega_1 \ln(1+z)$, where $z$ represents redshift and $\omega_0$, $\omega_1$ are constant parameters. We analyze the cosmological evolution of this model by examining its statefinder diagnostics, equation of state, and deceleration parameter. Furthermore, we explore the model's dynamical evolution through a system of autonomous equations. Our findings indicate that the model can accommodate both accelerating and decelerating phases of cosmic evolution, contingent upon the values of $\omega_0$ and $\omega_1$. Additionally, we demonstrate that the model can transition from a decelerating to an accelerating phase, or vice versa, depending on these parameters.

The detection of a radio burst from the tidal disruption event (TDE) AT2019qiz, occurring roughly 100 days post-disruption, has sparked significant interest. This study proposes a mechanism wherein the radio emission arises from synchrotron radiation generated by electrons accelerated at the shock front of the relativistic jet colliding with the ambient medium. We demonstrate that the jet's interaction with the surrounding environment creates a quasi-perpendicular shock, which efficiently accelerates particles to high energies. Furthermore, we show that the radio burst's observed characteristics can be explained by the synchrotron emission of these accelerated electrons. This work offers a viable explanation for the radio burst from AT2019qiz and establishes a framework for understanding similar phenomena in other TDEs.

This study examines the acoustic cavitation of microbubbles within a resonant state, utilizing a theoretical framework that incorporates the Rayleigh-Plesset equation alongside a model for the surrounding medium's pressure. The analysis focuses on the temporal evolution of bubble radius, specifically investigating the impact of varying initial conditions and driving parameters. The findings indicate that bubbles with an initial radius of 10 micrometers or less can achieve a maximum expansion of up to 100 micrometers when subjected to a 1 MHz driving frequency.

Tension detection in conversations is a critical component of social intelligence, yet it remains an under-explored area in research. This paper introduces a novel multimodal framework for identifying tension by leveraging emotion acknowledgment as a secondary auxiliary task. The architecture comprises two distinct modules: a primary tension identification module and a supplementary emotion acknowledgment module. The former utilizes multimodal features to predict tension, while the latter employs a multimodal transformer to forecast the emotional state of the responding speaker. This auxiliary module is designed to enhance the performance of the main task by providing contextual emotional cues. Furthermore, we propose a new loss function that integrates both tasks to facilitate their joint optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art approaches.

PanGEA is a toolkit designed for the annotation of expansive graphs, such as knowledge graphs, biological networks, and software dependency graphs. It offers a web-based interface for annotating graph nodes and edges, as well as a command-line tool for batch operations. PanGEA supports various data formats, including RDF, JSON-LD, and GEXF, and allows users to import graphs from external sources or create them within the system. It also facilitates the export of annotated data in multiple formats. PanGEA is open-source and freely available for use.

The "downsizing" phenomenon describes the shift in the epoch of peak star formation from massive to low-mass galaxies. This study investigates the role of the Initial Mass Function (IMF) in this process, specifically examining how IMF variations with galaxy mass and environment influence the timing of star formation peaks. We utilize a semi-analytical model of galaxy formation that incorporates an IMF dependent on both galaxy mass and environment, alongside a Supernova Ia (SNIa) rate linked to the star formation history. Our results indicate that accounting for IMF variations is essential for accurately reproducing the observed star formation rate (SFR) density evolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the SNIa rate, which depends on the star formation history, is critical for matching the observed evolution of the stellar mass density.

This study introduces a novel image compressive sensing (CS) reconstruction framework that leverages the collective sparse representation of images. The proposed method employs a non-linear regularization technique to enhance the sparsity of the CS transform domain coefficients. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed non-linear regularization scheme achieves a lower objective function value compared to existing linear approaches. Furthermore, experimental results indicate that the proposed method outperforms current state-of-the-art CS reconstruction techniques.

This study introduces RethNet, a neural network designed to identify skin problems in facial images. The model employs a two-stage approach: first, it utilizes a pre-trained face detector to locate and extract individual skin lesions, and second, it applies a convolutional neural network to classify these lesions. The system was evaluated on the Kaggle Facial Skin Issues dataset, achieving an F1 score of 0.71.

This paper examines the efficiency and complexity of sequential decoding for polar additive codes, which are a subset of polar codes. We demonstrate that PAC codes, which are a subset of polar additive codes, achieve the capacity of the binary-input additive channel. Furthermore, we show that the complexity of sequential decoding for these codes grows exponentially with the block length, a rate that is strictly lower than the complexity observed in standard polar codes.

Suggesting items to users who have no prior interaction history, known as the cold-start problem, remains a significant hurdle in recommender systems. While existing methods typically rely on collaborative filtering, they struggle to generate personalized recommendations for these new users. To address this, we introduce a novel approach that leverages sequential data to deliver tailored suggestions for cold-start scenarios. Our method utilizes a meta-learning framework to adapt the model for new users by learning from the sequential patterns of similar users. Furthermore, we propose a meta-transitional educational mechanism designed to mitigate the negative impact of sparse data inherent to cold-start conditions. Extensive experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques.

The origins of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) remain a significant unsolved issue in astrophysics. While the most favored hypothesis attributes these particles to extragalactic sources, a compelling alternative suggests they originate within our own Galaxy. This review examines the current status of research on galactic UHECRs, covering both the observational data and the theoretical frameworks. We explore the primary characteristics of the observed spectrum and composition, alongside the principal challenges in explaining them. Furthermore, we detail the foundational elements of galactic UHECR models, including the necessary source properties, propagation mechanisms, and the resulting predictions for the spectrum and elemental makeup. Finally, we highlight the most critical open questions and potential avenues for future investigation.

The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission aims to alter the orbital trajectory of the asteroid Dimorphos by colliding a spacecraft with it. This study examines how the projectile's shape influences the momentum transfer during the impact. We conducted numerical simulations of the DART impact using the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method, modeling the projectile as a sphere, a cube, and a rectangular parallelepiped. Our results indicate that the projectile's geometry significantly affects the momentum exchange, with the cube demonstrating the highest momentum transfer efficiency. This enhanced efficiency is attributed to the larger volume of the projectile's crater and the greater mass of the ejecta. Furthermore, we analyzed the crater's morphology and the distribution of the ejecta cloud to understand the underlying mechanisms driving these variations.

This paper introduces a new approach to operator recognition through vehicle windshields, addressing the challenge of capturing facial details obscured by glare, reflections, and obstructions. We propose MU-Net, a high-dynamic interval fusion network that integrates both spatial and temporal data. The architecture employs a dual-branch design: one branch processes the original image, while the other handles a high-dynamic range version generated by a proposed interval transformation. These branches are fused via a specialized module that merges spatial and temporal information. Experimental results demonstrate that MU-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance on the newly introduced THWIND dataset.

The Open Source Blurb Archive Network (OSBAN) is a proposed system designed to enhance the accessibility and utility of open-source programming language repositories. By aggregating and organizing metadata from these diverse platforms, OSBAN aims to create a centralized hub for developers to discover, evaluate, and utilize existing code. This paper outlines the initial design principles for OSBAN, focusing on key components such as data ingestion strategies, search functionality, and user interface design. We also explore potential applications of the system, including automated code discovery, performance benchmarking, and community-driven development. Finally, we discuss the challenges associated with implementing OSBAN, including issues related to data privacy, scalability, and maintaining up-to-date information.

This study addresses the challenge of estimating the average treatment effect (ATE) when covariates are missing for some participants and outcomes remain incomplete for others. We introduce a multistage estimation framework that leverages data from both the ATE analysis and the missingness mechanism to generate robust, semiparametric efficient estimators. Our approach is adaptable to various scenarios, including those with missing data under Missing at Random (MAR) conditions, non-ignorable missingness, and outcomes that are not Missing at Random (MNAR). We provide theoretical justification for the proposed estimators and validate their performance through simulations. Finally, we apply our methodology to estimate the impact of a job training program on earnings using data from the National Supported Work Demonstration.
This paper introduces a hypothesis concerning bounds for complete elliptic integrals of the first kind expressed as the inverse hyperbolic tangent.

This paper introduces a novel learning framework that decomposes the inductive method into two distinct components: a hypothesis generator and a hypothesis filter. While traditional approaches rely on a single inductive method to produce and evaluate hypotheses, our approach separates these tasks. The generator is responsible for creating a pool of candidate hypotheses, whereas the filter selects the most appropriate one from that set. This separation offers significant advantages, including the ability to utilize multiple generators to create a diverse range of hypotheses and the capacity to employ various filtering strategies. This flexibility allows for the development of new learning algorithms by combining different generators and filters. The study demonstrates this by constructing several algorithms using a single filter paired with different generators, as well as by combining multiple generators with a single filter. Furthermore, we present a hybrid algorithm that integrates both multiple generators and multiple filters.

The proliferation of fake news on social media has become a significant global concern, with its impact on the Arab world being particularly severe. This study introduces a novel machine learning framework designed to automatically detect and classify Arabic fake news. The proposed system integrates a hybrid approach combining deep learning and traditional machine learning techniques. The results demonstrate that this hybrid model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving an F1-score of 90.1% and a 90.1% accuracy rate. The source code for this system is publicly available at https://github.com/ahmed-ahmed1999/FakeNewsDetector.

Let $K$ represent the compositum of all $D_4$ extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$. In this paper, we establish the torsion subgroup structure for all elliptic curves defined over $K$ with rational coefficients. This work serves as a correction to a previous publication by the first author.

This study examines the dynamics of nonlocal relationships within a four-qubit system, specifically focusing on the interplay between nonlocality and entanglement. We analyze how these relationships evolve over time in a four-qubit setup subjected to amplitude damping, dephasing, and depolarizing noise. Our findings indicate that nonlocality can persist even when entanglement is completely eliminated. Additionally, we demonstrate that the degree of nonlocality is contingent upon the specific type of noise applied. To achieve this, we developed a matrix product operator (MPO) algorithm designed to simulate the dynamics of multiqubit systems under various noise conditions.

Scalable web scraping is essential for gathering data from the internet, yet it remains a difficult task due to the vast diversity of website structures. This paper introduces a reinforcement learning (RL) framework designed to automate the scraping of webpages by generating an optimal, tree-structured plan. This approach enables the efficient extraction of data from multiple pages sharing a similar layout. We developed a specific reward function to guide the RL agent toward creating a tree structure that maximizes data extraction. Experiments conducted on real-world webpages demonstrate that our method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in both the volume of data extracted and the reduction in total scraping costs.

This study introduces a new dataset designed to enhance the understanding of object-focused event information. It features 1,000 instances across 100 distinct event types, with each type represented by 10 examples. The data includes 100 corresponding images and 100 associated textual descriptions. The paper outlines the dataset's construction, its specific characteristics, and the associated challenges. Furthermore, it reports preliminary experimental outcomes and discusses potential future research avenues.

This study introduces a novel method for recovering wavefields from limited data, specifically addressing the challenge of missing spatial samples. The approach utilizes a weighted matrix decomposition technique, where weights are determined by the available data to ensure the reconstruction remains faithful to the input. The method is validated through numerical experiments involving both synthetic and real-world datasets.

Metalenses have garnered significant attention for their potential to revolutionize optical systems, yet their performance is often hindered by narrow bandwidths and restricted fields of view. This study introduces a novel metalens design that overcomes these limitations by employing a quadratic phase profile. This approach enables the lens to maintain a broad field of view while achieving a wide operational bandwidth. The lens is constructed using a silicon nitride substrate patterned with subwavelength silicon pillars. The design leverages a rigorous coupled-wave analysis to optimize the geometry of the pillars, ensuring a flat phase profile across the entire lens surface. The resulting device demonstrates a focal length of 15.4 µm and a half-angle field of view of 60°, with a central wavelength of 1550 nm. Furthermore, the lens exhibits a broad bandwidth, functioning effectively from 1300 nm to 1650 nm.

This study presents a two-dimensional simulation and modeling of a non-neutral plasma system formed by radio-frequency (RF) atmospheric pressure plasma streams. The research focuses on the dynamics of a plasma stream generated by a single RF electrode, specifically examining how it interacts with a second, identical electrode positioned nearby. The study investigates the influence of the distance between these electrodes on the resulting plasma stream characteristics. The findings indicate that the plasma stream exhibits a non-neutral nature, with its behavior being highly sensitive to the inter-electrode spacing.

This study investigates the quasinormal modes of $d$-dimensional black holes with string corrections, employing the eikonal limit. We demonstrate that the real component of these modes is governed by the effective potential's peak, whereas the imaginary part is determined by the black hole's silhouette.

Pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) are currently the most effective instruments for detecting gravitational waves (GWs) in the nanohertz frequency range. While the standard approach involves analyzing common-band stochastic processes, this study introduces a cross-correlation-based technique that utilizes data from multiple PTAs. This method leverages the cross-correlation between the GW signals recorded by different arrays, which is governed by the same Hellings-Inta correlation function. We demonstrate that this cross-correlation approach offers superior sensitivity to GW signals compared to the conventional common-band method. Furthermore, we outline a framework for estimating the cross-correlation function and its associated uncertainties, which can be applied to constrain the spectral index of a stochastic GW background.

This study introduces a new, straightforward, and efficient method for determining the weight distribution of generator matrices under support constraints. The approach is founded on the generalized Hadamard-Walsh transform (GHW transform), a technique previously established in [1]. We demonstrate that this method is both necessary and sufficient, and it is significantly more efficient than existing techniques.

This study investigates matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operators defined on model subspaces of the vector-valued $H^2$ space, utilizing symbols that are matrix-valued $L^{\infty}$ functions. We establish the operators' kernel and demonstrate that these operators are equivalent under unitary transformations if and only if their symbols are equivalent under a specific extension-defined relation.

This study examines Bayesian influence within a sequence of Bernoulli trials, where the probability of success is unknown and modeled using a Beta prior. We derive a closed-form expression for the expected absolute difference in posterior means between two scenarios: one where a specific outcome (success or failure) is observed, and another where it is not. We also analyze the asymptotic behavior of this influence metric. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Bayesian influence for the first trial exceeds that of subsequent trials, and we establish a closed-form expression for the cumulative influence across the first $n$ trials.

This study investigates the application of the Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) algorithm for unsupervised anomaly detection within audio data. The proposed methodology involves training a UMAP model on normal audio samples and subsequently projecting anomalous samples into the latent space derived from the normal data distribution. The resulting distances between these projected points are then evaluated to identify anomalies. The authors demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through experiments on the UrbanSound8K dataset, which comprises 10 distinct sound categories. The results indicate that UMAP effectively identifies anomalies, outperforming baseline methods such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE).

This study investigates the spectral characteristics of gamma-ray pulsars by analyzing 140 objects from the Fermi-LAT catalog. We employed a stacking technique to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio, enabling the detection of spectral features in individual pulsars that were previously obscured. Our findings reveal that gamma-ray pulsars exhibit a two-component structure: a power-law component and an exponential cutoff component. The power-law index for these sources ranges from 1.5 to 2.5, with an average of approximately 2.0. Furthermore, we identified a correlation between the power-law index and the spin-down luminosity, suggesting that the power-law component arises from synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) processes.

The fractional quantum Hall effect (FQHE) is a complex many-body phenomenon that has been extensively investigated over the past four decades. Despite significant progress, the underlying mechanism remains elusive. This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework for FQHE that relies on the concept of numerous magnetorotons. We demonstrate that the spectral total regulation (STR) principle, which governs the sum of spectral weights in the fractional quantum Hall regime, is a direct consequence of the magnetoroton concept. Furthermore, we propose that the magnetoroton concept can be extended to the integer quantum Hall effect (IQHE).

The Intense Energy Occurrences (IEO) experiment, a ground-based setup designed to measure the flux of high-energy gamma rays and cosmic rays, is situated at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa. Comprising two telescopes, the facility is optimized to detect particles with energies ranging from 100 GeV to 10 TeV. This paper details the performance of the IEO telescopes, specifically analyzing their energy resolution and angular resolution.

This study examines the performance of various machine learning classifiers when trained on datasets containing noisy labels. We evaluate both standard algorithms and a proposed method designed to mitigate label noise. Our analysis reveals that the new algorithm consistently surpasses existing approaches in accuracy across multiple datasets.

This paper examines the automorphism groups and inherent symmetries of cyclic orbit codes within the extension field $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We establish that the automorphism group of a cyclic orbit code forms a semi-direct product comprising a subgroup of the Galois group $\text{Gal}(\mathbb{F}_{q^n}/\mathbb{F}_q)$ and a specific cyclic subgroup of the multiplicative group $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^*$. Furthermore, we derive a formula for the code's symmetry count and demonstrate that cyclic orbit codes possess a symmetry count equivalent to that of cyclic codes.

We report the first precise mass determination for a turnoff star in the ancient open cluster M67, achieved by combining high-precision astrometry from the Gaia mission with precise transit timing data from the Kepler and K2 missions. This analysis utilizes a 10.5-year dataset of 1,000 transits from the K2 mission, covering the star KIC 8472219 (M67-100), which is located at the cluster's main sequence turnoff. By applying a Bayesian framework to the transit timing data, we derived the star's orbital period and transit duration, which were subsequently used to calculate the star's mass. This mass was then integrated with Gaia's parallax and proper motion measurements to determine the star's distance and transverse velocity. Our findings indicate that the star has a mass of $0.802 \pm 0.004\,M_\odot$, a distance of $1.59 \pm 0.02\,\text{kpc}$, and a transverse velocity of $1.5 \pm 0.2\,\text{km/s}$. These results confirm that the star is a member of M67 and provide a highly accurate measurement of its mass.

This paper examines the framework of eigenfunctions associated with the complex Schrödinger operator $\mathscr{L}_c=-d^2/dx^2+cx^\alpha$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}$ and $\alpha>0$. We establish a sufficiency theorem for the inverse spectral problem concerning the complex Schrödinger operator, demonstrating that the spectrum uniquely determines the potential $c x^\alpha$ within the class of functions $c\in\mathbb{C}$ and $\alpha>0$.

This study introduces a novel density-driven smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) framework designed to ensure the conservation of mass, momentum, and energy. The proposed method employs a superior gradient estimation technique that utilizes a local least-squares fit to the particle distribution function, combined with a modified partition of unity approach to guarantee conservation laws. The scheme's performance is validated through a series of benchmark tests, including the shock tube problem, the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability, and the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability under varying density ratios. The results demonstrate that this density-driven SPH method achieves significantly improved conservation properties compared to existing density-driven approaches.

This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to enhance the spectral resolution of hyperspectral images. The proposed method, termed the Deep Function-blend Network (DFN), integrates a deep neural network with a pixel-wise function blending technique. The core function blending mechanism utilizes a network to generate a pixel-specific blending function, which then combines the input low-resolution image with a high-resolution spectral estimate derived from the network. This approach offers superior flexibility compared to standard deep learning models, as it allows the network to adaptively determine the optimal balance between the original low-resolution data and the enhanced high-resolution prediction for each individual pixel. Experimental results demonstrate that the DFN outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality.

This paper introduces a new approach to object geotagging that integrates contextual information to enhance the precision of object detection. We propose a novel context-sensitive object geotagging framework that leverages contextual cues to refine detection accuracy. By employing a two-stage methodology, we first utilize a context-sensitive proposal generator to create region proposals, followed by a context-sensitive object geotagging module to classify and localize objects. We evaluate our method on the COCO dataset, demonstrating that it surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques.

The study introduces a novel approach to training deep learning models for dam detection and storage estimation using remote imagery. This method employs a custom metric that prioritizes the accurate identification of dam locations and the estimation of water volume, rather than relying on standard classification criteria. This strategy is particularly effective for scenarios where the dataset is imbalanced, a common issue in remote sensing applications. The proposed technique was evaluated on a dataset of 1,000 images featuring 1,000 dams, with the model trained using the custom metric. Results indicate that this method outperforms standard training approaches, achieving a 10% improvement in dam detection accuracy and a 15% improvement in storage estimation precision.
